properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/14/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Bell Township, Clearfield county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/14/2023
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8158551
Permit API: 033-25118
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Bell Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/14/2023
Comments: The Department received a complaint on 9/11/23 regarding a potential brine leak on the ground at conventional well 033-25118. I conducted a site inspection on 9/14/23. I observed a bare spot of soil inundated with deer hoof prints near the valve on the brine tank. An area of dead and/or stressed vegetation was also observed. In addition, some standing puddles were observed near the brine tank and in a ditch approximately 20' away from the brine tank. I screened the puddles using an Oakton meter for conductivity. Readings ranged from 16.93 mS/cm to 4.23 mS/cm. A grab sample was collected (3442-696) from one of the puddles near the brine tank and was sent to the Departments lab in Harrisburg to be tested for SAC 942 plus aluminum, bromide, and lithium. Based off screenings and dead vegetation the impacted area is at 20' x20'. After leaving the site I contacted Heather Empfield and Mark McCracken of Diversified and reported my findings. The Department recommends that operator investigates the brine release and based off the amount of brine released, the operator addresses the remediation in accordance with small spill policy 800-5000-001 or Act 2.Violations have been citied.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/27/2026 to BIG DOG ENERGY LLC in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland county. 78a64a(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Well site was not designed and constructed using secondary containment.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BIG DOG ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/27/2026
Violation Code: 78a64a(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Well site was not designed and constructed using secondary containment.
Violation ID: 8272095
Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/27/2026
Comments: On 4/27/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. Present were Rosie Wise (DEP Environmental Trainee) and myself. This inspection follows up to IR 4168852, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed during the inspection:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (photos 4, 6, and 7). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (photo 10). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (photos 3 and 11). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team. The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (photos 9 and 12). A violation was issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C). The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photos 5 and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4168852 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Permit API: 129-28077
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/02/2025
Comments: On April 2, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. All other production equipment appeared removed.It appeared excavation had been conducted in the area where the production equipment was removed, as well as the ditch from behind the production equipment area to where the boom was installed. Excavated material/soil appeared loaded onto plastic liners and covered with additional liners.A background soil conductivity was taken with a reading of 0.20mS. Soil conductivity reading were taken in the area where the production tank was previously located with readings of 0.86mS, and 0.65mS. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel behind the production equipment area. Conductivity readings were taken in the ditch in several locations with readings of 0.76mS, 0.64mS, 0.814mS, and 0.47mS.No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. A conductivity reading was taken in this area of the ditch with a reading of 0.55mSA conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.67mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream. It does not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.The Department recommends the operator promptly install/implement temporary erosion and sediment controls. The Department also recommends the operator temporarily stabilize any disturbed areas with in 4 days following cessation of earth disturbance activities.Based on today's inspection, violation remain outstanding as a notice of intent to conduct Act 2 remediation has not yet been received by the Department.

Report Details

Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2026
Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, and 4157162. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports. The narrative of both inspection reports are identical except for references to photos. This is inspection 1 of 2. A COA with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced.This inspection is being conducted with Aquatic Biologist 2s Christy Owens (DEP) and Miles Hegedus (DEP) to identify possible streams and wetland along the access road.Culvert 1 crossing (Photos 1-2) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The outlet appears to be blocked due to soil moved during access road clearing.Culvert 2 crossing (P 3-4) appears to be a stream crossing. The outlet to the culvert appears to be blocked.Culvert 3 crossing (P 5-7) appears to be a stream crossing. The inlet to the culvert appears to be blocked.Culvert 4 crossing (P 8-9) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch, however this culvert is not receiving water at this time due to the operator disturbing the channel causing water to be diverted further down the access road (P 10-12). The source of the water appears to be due to a seep which is causing early stages of wetland formation. The disturbed channel appears to be carrying fine sediment (Photos 10-11) towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen.Culvert 5 crossing (P 13-15) appears to be a stream crossing. E and S off of the access road was observed during the previous inspection earlier today above the outlet at culvert 5, however no sediment is observed entering the stream at this time.Just past culvert 5 on the inlet side appears to be a wetland (P 16).Culvert 6 crossing (P 17-19) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The inlet of the culvert appears to be partially blocked. E and S off of the access road was observed during the previous inspection earlier today above the outlet at culvert 6. The erosion and sedimentation at this area appears to stop near the end of the culvert.Culvert 7 crossing (P 20-21) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The inlet appears to be partially blocked and the outlet cannot be seen at this time due to brush.Culvert 8 crossing (P 22-25) appears to be a stream crossing. CFS is observed to be installed and functioning properly above the inlet side of the culvert. Upstream from the inlet of the stream and near the soil stockpile in this area, the Department observed newly moved soil that has been pushed into the stream channel.The Department recommends the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5 (P 8, 10-12, 16).The Department recommends removing sediment from the stream channel at culvert 8.The Department recommends the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.Violations were issued in IR 4157087 for accelerated E and S, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts in an inspection that was conducted earlier today prior to this inspection with Department Biologists. Therefore these violations are not included in this inspection report.New violations are being issued for sediment discharge into a stream, impact to wetland, and failing to identify wetlands and streams on the E and S plans.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On May 7, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Cowden 11H OG Well located on the Cowden 15 well pad in Hopewell Township, Washington County following IR 4139773, where violations were issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan on site. Present at the time of today's inspection is Big Dog Energy (BDE) representatives Chris McNichols and Matt Kuhn. BDE is reportedly the agent intending to operate the gas wells on the Cowden 15 well pad, however, according to Department records, Diversified owns both the well pad and the gas wells on this well pad. However, there is a pending transfer of ownership from Diversified to BDE. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance, all information that is required to be posted on the Act 9 sign appears to be BDE's. Both on-site mailboxes which were attached to the Act 9 sign were observed to be empty at the time of this inspection. While on-site, the Department spoke with Mr. Kuhn and Mr. McNichols, who both were unaware of when the ERP would be available on site. Mr. McNichols prompted Mr. Kuhn call and inquire about the status of the ERP, however, the Department was not made aware of any potential updates regarding the ERP while on-site. Violations issued for failure to have the ERP on site are being continued at this time.During IR 4166726, the Department requested a schedule is provided to the Department when the ERP will be available on site by COB 4/08/2026. IR 4198168 documents the receipt of an email the Department received on 4/07/2026 from BDE representative Matthew Anderson, which stated "As we stated our ERPs and some signage was stolen. We are having new ones written up and sign ordered. The unused equipment will be in use soon." However, a schedule of when the ERP would be available was not provided.At the time of this inspection, the Department inquired with Mr. McNichols, whether any wells on the Cowden 15 well site are in production yet (the 11H, 12H, and 15H). Mr. McNichols stated that the wells on the Cowden 15 pad were "flowing to the pipeline". At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the 11H gas well to be surrounded by cement barriers and had a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of this gas well. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a separator, 2 GPUs, and 3 green production tanks within secondary containment, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment. A white above ground storage tank was also observed to be on site, that was previously not connected for production, however, at the time of this inspection, Mr. McNichols stated that this white tank is now connected to the gas wells on the Cowden 15 pad. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. Based on today's inspection, violations issued to the 11H gas well for a lack of an Emergency Response Plan on site is to remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: On June 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Cowden 6H gas well located on the Cowden 16 well pad in Hopewell Twp, Washington Co. (Due to database error, this inspection report lists the Farm Name and Well # as the Cowden 9H OG Well) following IR 4139756, where violations were issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan on site and failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad.Big Dog Energy is reportedly the agent intending to operate the gas wells on the Cowden 16 well pad, however, according to DEP records, Diversified owns both the gas wells on the pad and the well pad. During this inspection, the following was observed:An Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance, all information that is required to be posted on the Act 9 sign appears to be BDE's. Both on-site mailboxes which were attached to the Act 9 sign were observed to be empty at the time of this inspection. (Photos 1-3). Violations issued for failure to have an ERP on site are being continued at this time.A graveled access road was observed to lead to the Cowden 16 gas well pad. No erosion and sedimentation issues were observed.The Cowden 16 gas well pad is located behind a chain-linked fence that was locked at the time of this inspection, therefore, the remainder of this inspection was conducted from outside of the chain-linked fence. (Photo 4).3 gas wells and 1 plugged gas well monument was observed on the Cowden 16 well pad (Photos 5-8). Equipment that was previously observed to be on the well pad and not connected for production appears to be removed from the well site at time. However, the white storage tank that was previously observed to be on site and not connected for production was still observed to be on the Cowden 16 well pad. Therefore, violations issued for failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for production of the well(s) are being continued at this time. (Photos 9-12).Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan on site and failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad are being continued for the 6H gas well at this time.

Comments: Results from sample IDs 0718-020 through 022, collected on 5/13/19 as documented in inspection report 2879933, were received from the lab on 6/21/19. At the time of inspection, WQS Sara Metz observed water discharging from the pad into the infiltration basin. Conductivity of the discharge ranged from 0.999 to 1.669 mS/cm, and conductivity in the basin where the discharge was entering was 1.493 mS/cm. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides in sample 0718-020, collected from the infiltration basin, indicate that the discharge was a pollutional substance. The discharge of a pollutional substance to the infiltration basin, considered Waters of the Commonwealth, is a violation of Section 401 of the Clean Streams Law. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides in sample 0718-021, collected from a high-conductivity puddle (18.75 mS/cm) on the pad near a crushed containment berm, also indicate a release of a pollutional substance to the pad surface (as compared to sample 0718-022 collected from an area of the pad containing water with conductivity under 1 mS/cm). It is unclear whether this affected area is separate from or related to the affected area described in a previous Notice of Violation issued on 6/10/19 with inspection report 2890742. Results from sample IDs 0718-024 through 028, collected on 5/17/19 as documented in inspection report 2885414, were also received from the lab on 6/21/19. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides were present in samples collected from the infiltration basin (0718-024) and the basin outfall pipe (0718-025). Additional samples collected from a PVC drain pipe discharge (0718-026) and the resulting flow path to Salt Spring Run (0718-027) show elevated levels of strontium and chlorides, as compared to background conditions in Salt Spring Run upstream of the pad location (0718-028). New violation noted. In addition, the following violations cited on 6/10/19 remain outstanding: 78a.66(b), 78a.56(a), Section 402(b) of the Clean Streams Law, and Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act.

Comments: On Thursday, 4/6/2023, I conducted a compliance evaluation inspection of the Diversified Production, LLC McIntyre 1 well, permit number 005-29235. The well is located in the woods off of Coal Bank Road in Gilpin township, Armstrong county. The previous inspection, inspection id # 3472682, conducted on 12/14/2022, resulted in violations being cited due to a broken pipe from the separator to the brine tank. Violations to 25 PA Code 78.54, 25 PA Code 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and CSL 402(b) were cited as a result of these conditions. The operator has collected the contaminated soils in 5 gallon buckets that remain onsite. The violations to SWMA 301 and SWMA 302(A) remain outstanding as a result of the operator's failure to remove and properly dispose of the contaminated soil, and provide proof of proper disposal to the Department, as was requested in the previous inspection report. The operator has placed stone/gravel onto an area of the access road, stabilizing an area of standing/ponded water noted in the previous inspection, correcting this deficiency. There are no new violations being cited for this inspection. The violations to SWMA 301 and SWMA 302(A) remain outstanding.

Comments: On 02/11/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the Veres Well Pad in Greene Township, Greene County following notification of a spill that occurred on 2/11/2026 from Greylock. I received a call from Trevor Wood, a representative from Greylock notifying me of the spill. I responded to the incident prior to it being assigned to Oil and Gas in our complaint system. I was accompanied by Keith from Greylock onsite. Per Greylock, the spill was reported to the Department's emergency hotline on 02/11/2026. It was reported that 1-3 bbls of produced water from a truck was released onto the pad on 02/11/2026. The spill was identified at 8:50 AM and reported to the hotline at approximately 9:43 AM. No waters of the Commonwealth were impacted.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan was onsite at the site entrance (Photo 1).The access road appeared to be in generally good condition and maintained (Photo 2).The spill occurred when a water truck was drawing down produced water from tank. It was believed a pump failed which caused produced water to spray onto the pad, tank and along tank containment. The area impacted was approximately 20ft by 20ft. 1-3 barrels (bbls) were released (Photos 3-6).A conductivity reading was taken in the middle of the impacted area and read 9.09 mS/cm. (Photo 7). Conductivity reading taken in gravel adjacent to separators in front of the tanks was 5.90 mS/cm (Photo 8, 9).I did not observe any spray on the backside of the tanks looking toward the spill area (Photo 10). The area was still in the process of remediation and Greylock was waiting on additional equipment to begin remediation. The spill appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. I recommend following Act 2 guidelines.Due to the release of produced water violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, and 91.34(a).

Comments: On 8/10/23 at 1201 hrs., I conducted an incident inspection of Madtick Development Corp.'s Musser Associates 2 well site (API 063-32934) in East Mahoning Twp., Indiana Co. The inspection was conducted in response to a phone call received on 8/10/23 from the landowner, indicating that a production fluid release was observed at the well site. The landowner unsuccessfully attempted to contact the operator, and then reported the release to the Department. Upon inspection of the site, stressed/dead vegetation was observed around the production fluid tank onsite, and in an adjacent corn field. The area of dead vegetation appears to be approximately 30-45 feet wide and extends approximately 200-250 feet to the North of the well site. The release appears to be originating from a tank onsite. The tank appears to be empty. The release appears to be over 1 barrel of fluid. In addition to the release, it was observed that the well is equipped for production. A well tag is not affixed to the completed well. A site ID sign is posted, but is illegible and does not display the required information.Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), and 78.66(b) are being cited for failure by the operator to report the release, and are immediately being closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of OGA 3211(G) and OGA 3211(H) are cited for the lack of site ID sign and well tag. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1) are cited for the release of production fluids from the tank onto the ground. The violations will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release anddemonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.
